content: We first encode both the question - $H_Q = encoder(Q)$, and the input - $H_I = encoder(I)$, separately using encoders (with shared weights). Then, to condition $I$ on $Q$ (and vice versa), we use the coattention encoder BIBREF10 which attends to both the $I$ and $Q$ simultaneously to generates the coattention context - $C_D = coatt(H_I, H_Q)$. Finally, using the pointer-generator decoder we find the probability distribution of the output sequence - $P(w) = decoder_{pg}([H_I; C_D])$, which is then decoded to generate the answer sequence.
